key_insight: On-Policy Context Distillation (OPCD) trains a student on its own generated contexts and aligns it to a context-conditioned teacher by minimizing reverse KL, allowing the model to internalize in‑context knowledge into its parameters.
problem_solved: Bridges the distribution mismatch between teacher-generated contexts and student usage: existing context distillation methods struggle to transfer in‑context (experiential) knowledge effectively into model parameters, limiting generalization and requiring large prompts or teacher rollouts.
method: On-policy rollouts: the student generates its own context-conditioned trajectories to train on the distributions it will actually encounter.

Reverse KL alignment: minimize KL(student || teacher) between student-generated conditionals and a context-conditioned teacher to encourage the student to match teacher behavior while using its own outputs.

Context-conditioned teacher targets: use a teacher that provides conditional distributions given contexts so the student internalizes experiential knowledge into weights rather than relying on external prompts.
impact: Enables language models to absorb in-context knowledge into model weights, reducing reliance on long prompting or teacher rollouts and improving sample efficiency for downstream tasks and model compression/fine-tuning workflows.

paper_title: On-Policy Context Distillation for Language Models
